examples.en: The school doesn't allow cell phone use.
The city denied permission for the building work.
I don't know why the company refused the vacation.
The court will turn down that application.
The concert hall does not permit filming.

examples.ko: 사진 촬영을 불허하면 안내문을 붙여야 해요.
examples.en: If you don't allow photography, you have to post a notice.

explain: '허락하다'의 반대로 규칙이나 기관이 공식적으로 안 된다고 정하는 느낌이에요. 친구나 가족 사이에서는 '안 돼요', '못 하게 해요'라고 말해요. 공지·뉴스에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: The opposite of 허락하다, with the feeling that a rule or institution officially says no. Among friends and family people say 안 돼요 or 못 하게 해요 instead. You see it often in notices and news.

examples.en: In our country, judicial power belongs to the courts.
The independence of the judiciary is very important for democracy.
The courts, not the police, exercise judicial power.

examples.ko: 정부가 사법권에 간섭하면 안 된다는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article saying the government must not interfere with the judiciary.

examples.ko: 입법권, 행정권, 사법권을 합쳐서 삼권이라고 해요.
examples.en: Legislative, executive, and judicial power together are called the three branches.

examples.ko: 사법권이 약한 나라에서는 재판이 불공정하다는 말이 나와요.
examples.en: In countries where judicial power is weak, people say trials are unfair.

explain: '입법권', '행정권'과 함께 삼권 분립 이야기에서 짝으로 나와요. 사회 수업이나 뉴스에서 '사법권의 독립'처럼 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It appears alongside '입법권' and '행정권' when talking about the separation of powers. You often hear it in social studies and news in phrases like '사법권의 독립' (independence of the judiciary).

examples.ko: 이 사안은 대표님께 먼저 보고해야 해요.
examples.en: This matter has to be reported to the CEO first.

examples.ko: 중요한 사안이라서 회의를 다시 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: It is an important matter, so we decided to hold another meeting.
Everyone knows how serious the issue is.

examples.ko: 법원이 이번 사안을 조심스럽게 검토하고 있어요.
examples.en: The court is carefully reviewing this case.
Keep a record even of a small matter.

examples.ko: 두 가지 사안을 따로 다루면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: It would be good to handle the two issues separately.

explain: 사안은 회의나 법원, 뉴스에서 다루는 일이나 문제를 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '일'이나 '문제'가 더 자연스러워요. 보통 '중요한 사안', '민감한 사안'처럼 꾸밈말이 앞에 와요.
explain_en: 사안 refers to a matter dealt with in meetings, courts or the news. In daily talk 일 or 문제 is more natural. It usually has a modifier before it, as in '중요한 사안' (important matter) or '민감한 사안' (sensitive matter).

en: be inherited; be passed down by inheritance

examples.en: The house was passed down to the son.
The property is inherited equally by the children.
When the company passed to his daughter, its name changed.

examples.ko: 유언이 없으면 재산은 법에 따라 상속될 거예요.
examples.en: Without a will, the property will be inherited according to law.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 오래전에 할아버지께 상속된 거예요.
examples.en: This land was inherited from my grandfather long ago.
Tax is charged on inherited property.

explain: 상속되다는 재산이나 권리가 법에 따라 사람에게서 사람에게 넘어갈 때 써서 집, 땅, 회사 같은 대상과 함께 나와요. 성격이나 얼굴이 닮는 것은 '유전되다', 전통이 이어지는 것은 '전해지다'라고 해요. 받는 사람 쪽은 '상속받다'를 써요.
explain_en: 상속되다 is for property or rights passing legally from one person to another, so it goes with houses, land and companies. Looks and personality passed on are 유전되다, and traditions handed down are 전해지다. From the receiver's side you say 상속받다.

examples.en: I got tax documents at the tax office.
You have to go to the tax office to register a business.
The tax office opens at nine on weekdays.
The tax office is close to my home.
A tax office employee explained kindly.
I have to send the documents to the tax office.

explain: 세무서는 세금을 걷고 신고를 받는 곳이에요. 신고를 대신해 주는 사람은 '세무사'라서 서로 달라요. 요즘은 '홈택스'로 인터넷에서도 신고해요. 주소나 증명서 일은 '구청'이나 '주민센터'에서 해요.
explain_en: 세무서 is where taxes are collected and returns are filed. The person who files for you is a 세무사, which is different. These days people also file online through 홈택스. Address and certificate matters go to the 구청 or 주민센터.

examples.en: The new law applies retroactively back to last month.
I received the raised salary retroactively back to March.

examples.ko: 이 규정을 과거 사건에 소급하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't apply this rule retroactively to past cases.

examples.ko: 환불 규정을 소급할 수 있는지 문의했어요.
examples.en: I asked whether the refund policy can be applied retroactively.

examples.ko: 소급하는 방식에 대해 직원들의 의견이 갈렸어요.
examples.en: Employees' opinions were divided on the retroactive approach.
The company decided not to apply the compensation retroactively.

explain: 법, 규정, 금액 같은 것이 지나간 시점까지 거슬러 올라가 적용될 때 써요. 보통 '소급 적용'이라는 말로 많이 들리고, 월급 인상이나 새 규정 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '거슬러 올라가다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a law, rule or amount is applied going back to an earlier point in time. You often hear it as '소급 적용', especially in talk of pay raises or new regulations. In daily speech, people also say '거슬러 올라가다'.

examples.en: The court sent a summons notice to the witness.
He answered the prosecutors' summons.
In the game, I learned a monster summoning skill.

examples.ko: 소환 날짜가 바뀌어서 일정을 다시 잡았어요.
examples.en: The summons date changed, so I rescheduled.
The news said the ambassador had been recalled to his home country.

examples.ko: 소환에 응하지 않으면 체포될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't comply with the summons, you can be arrested.

explain: 법원이나 검찰이 사람을 정해진 곳으로 부를 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요. 일상에서 '부르다'는 아무나 쓰지만 소환은 공식 기관이 쓸 때 가장 자연스러워요. 요즘은 게임에서 캐릭터를 불러올 때도 '소환'이라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is the official word for a court or prosecutor calling a person to a set place. Anyone can use '부르다' in daily life, but 소환 is most natural from an official body. These days it is also widely used in games for calling up characters.

examples.en: A summons arrived from the court yesterday.

examples.ko: 소환장을 받으면 정해진 날짜에 출석해야 해요.
examples.en: If you receive a summons, you must appear on the set date.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 소환장을 무시하고 나타나지 않았어요.
examples.en: He ignored the summons and did not show up.
They say the police sent a summons to the witness.

examples.ko: 우편함에 소환장 같은 서류가 들어 있어서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised to find a document like a summons in the mailbox.

examples.ko: 소환장에 적힌 시간에 맞춰 법원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the court at the time written on the summons.

explain: '소환장을 받다/보내다/발부하다'처럼 써요. 법원이나 검찰에서 오는 공식 서류라서 일상 대화보다 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '소환장을 받다/보내다/발부하다'. Because it is an official document from a court or prosecutors' office, you meet it more in the news than in daily talk.

examples.en: The court summoned the witness.
The police will summon that person.
A summons letter came to my house.
I summon a new character in the game.
The National Assembly decided to summon the CEO.

examples.ko: 그 마법사는 불의 정령을 소환하려고 주문을 외웠어요.
examples.en: The wizard recited a spell to summon a fire spirit.

explain: 수사나 재판에서 사람을 불러 오게 할 때 '소환하다'를 써요. 일상에서 사람을 부를 때는 '부르다'를 써요. 게임이나 판타지에서 캐릭터를 불러낼 때도 '소환하다'를 써요.
explain_en: In investigations and trials, it is the verb for ordering someone to appear. In daily life you just use '부르다' (call). It is also used for calling up characters in games and fantasy stories.

examples.en: Thanks to the lawyer, we won the trial.

examples.ko: 이번 승소는 회사에 큰 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: This court win was a big help to the company.
Everyone was happy to hear the news of the win in court.
The chance that we will win the case is not high.
If you win the case, you can receive compensation.

examples.ko: 작은 가게가 대기업과의 소송에서 승소를 거뒀어요.
examples.en: A small shop won its lawsuit against a large corporation.

explain: 반대말은 '패소'예요. 소송이나 재판에서만 써서 일상 대화에서는 드물고, 뉴스에서 '~이 승소했다'로 자주 들려요. 시합이나 게임에서 이기는 건 '이기다', '승리하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is 패소. It is used only for lawsuits and trials, so it is rare in everyday talk, but you often hear '~이 승소했다' in the news. For winning a match or a game, use 이기다 or 승리하다.

examples.en: The police search and seizure began in the morning.
Confiscated items are kept in a warehouse.
Items that were seized are hard to get back.

examples.ko: 시험 중 휴대전화 압수는 학교 규칙이에요.
examples.en: Confiscating phones during exams is a school rule.
The shop owner was flustered by the sudden seizure.
Seizures of illegal copies are increasing.

explain: 압수는 경찰이나 학교처럼 권한이 있는 쪽이 물건을 가져가는 일이에요. 뉴스에서는 '압수 수색'이라고 한 덩어리로 자주 나와요. 훔치는 것과 달리 법이나 규칙에 따라 가져간다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: 압수 is used when someone with authority, such as the police or a school, takes an item away. In the news it often appears as the set phrase 압수 수색. Unlike stealing, it is done under a law or rule.

examples.en: The teacher confiscated the game console during class.
Customs confiscated the fruit in the bag.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어기면 물건을 압수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you break the rules, your things can be confiscated.
The police seized the computer and investigated.
They give back confiscated items later.

examples.ko: 부모님이 제 휴대폰을 압수해서 연락을 못 했어요.
examples.en: My parents took my phone away, so I couldn't get in touch.

explain: '압수하다'는 가져가는 사람이 경찰, 세관, 선생님처럼 권한이 있는 사람이에요. 친구끼리 장난으로 뺏을 때는 '뺏다'를 써요. 뺏기는 쪽은 '압수당하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The one doing 압수하다 is someone with authority, such as the police, customs, or a teacher. When friends take something playfully, they use 뺏다. The person it is taken from says 압수당하다.

examples.ko: 이혼할 때 아이의 양육권을 누가 갖는지 정해야 해요.
examples.en: When parents divorce, they have to decide who gets custody of the child.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 양육권 문제로 오래 다퉜어요.
examples.en: The two of them argued for a long time over the custody issue.
The court granted custody to the mother.
Can the father also demand custody?
A custody lawsuit takes a long time.

examples.ko: 아이가 클 때까지 양육권은 엄마가 가지기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided that the mother would have custody until the child grows up.

explain: 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 '이혼', '친권', '소송'과 같이 자주 나와요. 보통 '양육권을 갖다', '양육권을 얻다', '양육권을 주장하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It often appears in news and legal talk together with words like '이혼' (divorce), '친권' (parental authority) and '소송' (lawsuit). It is usually used as '양육권을 갖다', '양육권을 얻다' or '양육권을 주장하다'.

examples.ko: 시민들은 사기 범죄에 대한 엄벌을 요구했어요.
examples.en: Citizens demanded severe punishment for fraud.

examples.ko: 이런 범죄는 엄벌에 처해야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think crimes like this should be severely punished.

examples.ko: 엄벌만이 해결책은 아니라고 말하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say that harsh punishment alone is not the solution.

examples.ko: 정부는 개인 정보를 판 업체에 엄벌 방침을 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government announced a policy of severe punishment for companies that sold personal data.

examples.ko: 판결이 나오자 엄벌을 바라던 가족들이 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: When the verdict came out, the families who had hoped for harsh punishment cried.

examples.ko: 회사 비밀을 지키지 않으면 엄벌이 따라요.
examples.en: If you don't keep company secrets, severe punishment follows.

explain: 뉴스와 판결 이야기에서 '엄벌에 처하다', '엄벌을 요구하다'처럼 자주 나와요. 반대되는 느낌의 말은 '선처'예요.
explain_en: It appears often in news and court stories in phrases like '엄벌에 처하다' and '엄벌을 요구하다'. A word with the opposite feeling is '선처' (leniency).

examples.ko: 정부는 불법 행위를 엄중히 처벌하겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government said it will punish illegal acts severely.

examples.ko: 회사는 이번 일을 엄중히 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is handling this matter very seriously.

examples.ko: 선생님이 시험 중 부정행위를 엄중히 경고하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher sternly warned against cheating during the exam.

examples.ko: 경찰이 엄중히 경계하는 가운데 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: The event took place under tight security by the police.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어긴 사람에게 엄중히 책임을 묻기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to hold those who broke the rules strictly responsible.
This problem has to be taken very seriously.

explain: '엄하게'와 비슷하지만 뉴스, 공문, 공식 발표에서 '엄중히 경고하다/처벌하다/대응하다'처럼 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서 혼내는 상황에는 '엄하게', '따끔하게'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '엄하게', but it shows up more in news, official documents and announcements, as in '엄중히 경고하다', '처벌하다' and '대응하다'. For scolding someone in daily life, '엄하게' or '따끔하게' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이사장이 한 번 더 연임하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The chairman decided to serve one more consecutive term.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 대표는 세 번이나 연임했어요.
examples.en: That company's CEO served three consecutive terms.

examples.ko: 이 단체의 회장은 연임할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The head of this organization cannot serve consecutive terms.
To serve another term, you need approval from the shareholders' meeting.

examples.ko: 시장이 연임해서 도시 계획이 계속 이어질 거예요.
examples.en: The mayor is serving another term, so the city plan will continue.

examples.ko: 원래 연임하는 사람이 드물어서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: People who serve consecutive terms are rare, so it became a talking point.

explain: 주어가 그 직책을 맡는 사람이고, '대표가 연임하다'처럼 써요. 선거나 승인을 거쳐 다음 임기를 이어서 맡는 느낌이에요. 뉴스에서는 '연임에 성공하다'처럼 명사 형태도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The subject is the person holding the post, as in '대표가 연임하다'. It feels like continuing into the next term after an election or approval. In the news the noun form also appears a lot, such as '연임에 성공하다'.

en: reservist; retired soldier in reserve status

examples.en: My father is a reserve army colonel.
My brother was discharged last year, so he is in the reserves now.

examples.ko: 예비역 모임에서 오랜만에 옛 전우들을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my old comrades after a long time at the reservists' gathering.

examples.ko: 예비역 장교들이 학교에서 안보 강연을 했어요.
examples.en: Reserve officers gave a talk on national security at the school.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 예비역이라서 예비군 훈련 때문에 이틀 동안 휴가를 냈어요.
examples.en: My uncle is a reservist, so he took two days off for his reserve training.

examples.ko: 예비역이 되면 일 년에 한두 번 훈련을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Once you become a reservist, you have to take part in training once or twice a year.

explain: 반의어는 '현역'이에요. '예비역 대령'처럼 계급 앞에 붙이거나 '예비역이에요'처럼 신분을 말할 때 써요. 예비역이 받는 훈련은 '예비군 훈련'이라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '현역' (active duty). It goes before a rank, as in '예비역 대령', or states someone's status, as in '예비역이에요'. The training reservists receive is often called '예비군 훈련'.

examples.ko: 교통 법규 위반자는 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: Traffic law violators have to pay a fine.
The police are looking for the rule violator.
A notice is stuck on the car of the parking violator.
I heard they stepped up enforcement because violators kept increasing.
The list of violators was posted online.

examples.ko: 마스크 규정 위반자는 입장할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Those who violate the mask rule cannot enter.

explain: 주로 법, 규칙, 규정을 어긴 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. '교통 법규 위반자'처럼 앞에 어긴 내용을 붙이는 경우가 많고, 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '규칙을 어긴 사람'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for a person who broke a law, rule or regulation. It often comes with what was broken, like '교통 법규 위반자', and you see it in news and notices. In daily talk people also say '규칙을 어긴 사람'.

examples.en: That action is illegal by law.
I heard the company made money in an illegal way.
The lawyer said this contract is illegal.
The police are cracking down on illegal parking.

examples.ko: 몰래 찍은 영상이 위법할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A video taken secretly can be illegal.
The ad was taken down right away because it was illegal.

explain: '위법하다'는 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '불법이다'가 더 흔하고, '위법'은 법의 규칙을 어겼다는 점을 따질 때 어울려요. '위법을 하다'보다 '위법한 행동'처럼 꾸미는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 위법하다 appears mostly in news and legal talk. In daily life 불법이다 is more common, while 위법 fits when you discuss whether a legal rule was broken. It often shows up as a modifier, like 위법한 행동.

examples.en: The government approved the founding of the new school.

examples.ko: 교육청이 이 학원을 정식으로 인가하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The education office decided to officially approve this institute.

examples.ko: 인가하지 않은 업체는 영업할 수 없어요.
examples.en: A business that has not been authorized cannot operate.

examples.ko: 시청에서 인가한 행사만 광장에서 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only events authorized by city hall can be held in the square.
Once the committee approves the plan, construction starts.

examples.ko: 담당 부서가 곧 사업을 인가할 거라고 했어요.
examples.en: The department in charge said it will approve the project soon.

explain: '허락하다'는 누구에게나 쓰지만 '인가하다'는 국가나 관청이 공식으로 인정해 줄 때 써요. 학교·학원·병원·단체 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 주어가 보통 정부나 관청이에요.
explain_en: '허락하다' works between anyone, but '인가하다' is used when a state or public office gives official approval. It often appears with schools, institutes, hospitals, and organizations, and the subject is usually the government or an office.

dis.h: authority grants permission or a license

p.n: 공인하다 does not fit with 'permitting the founding of a school'; it means recognizing something as official or valid.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 저작물이라서 허락 없이 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This photo is a copyrighted work, so you can't use it without permission.

examples.ko: 다른 사람의 저작물을 쓸 때는 출처를 꼭 밝히세요.
examples.en: When you use someone else's work, be sure to give the source.
My work was spread around the internet without permission.

examples.ko: 저작물 이용 허락을 받으려고 출판사에 메일을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I emailed the publisher to get permission to use the work.
The creator holds the rights to a work.

examples.ko: 음악, 영화, 책은 모두 저작물에 들어가요.
examples.en: Music, films and books all count as creative works.

explain: 책, 음악, 그림, 사진처럼 사람이 만든 창작물을 법적으로 부르는 말이에요. '저작권', '저작물 이용'처럼 법이나 계약 이야기에서 써요. 일상에서는 '작품'이 더 가볍게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is the legal term for things people create, such as books, music, pictures and photos. It appears in legal and contract talk, as in '저작권' (copyright) and '저작물 이용' (use of a work). In daily speech '작품' feels lighter.

dis.h: a creative work protected by copyright

p.n: 저작 is more about the writing or authorship than the legal object.

examples.en: This transaction is completely legal.
They made the arrest through lawful procedures.
I asked a lawyer whether that method is legal.

examples.ko: 허가 없이 찍은 사진은 적법하지 않아요.
examples.en: Photos taken without permission are not lawful.
If it had been legal, it wouldn't have been a problem.
The money was earned legally, so I'm not worried.

explain: 적법하다는 뉴스, 재판, 계약서처럼 딱딱한 자리에서 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '합법이에요'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '위법하다'예요. '적법한 절차', '적법하게'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 적법하다 is used mostly in formal settings such as news, trials, and contracts. In daily talk, 합법이에요 sounds more natural. The opposite is 위법하다. It often appears in forms that modify what follows, like 적법한 절차 and 적법하게.

examples.ko: 불법 점유는 처벌을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Illegal occupation can be punished.

examples.ko: 회의실 점유 시간을 한 시간으로 정했어요.
examples.en: We set the meeting room occupancy time to one hour.

examples.ko: 가게 앞 인도 점유 때문에 불편하다는 민원이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many complaints that the shop's use of the sidewalk is inconvenient.

examples.ko: 사무실 점유 기간이 이번 달 말까지예요.
examples.en: The office occupancy period runs through the end of this month.

examples.ko: 점유와 소유는 다르다고 법 수업에서 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned in law class that possession and ownership are different.

examples.ko: 그 땅의 점유가 누구에게 있는지 아직 몰라요.
examples.en: I still don't know who is in possession of that land.

explain: 점유는 실제로 차지해서 쓰고 있는 상태, 소유는 법적으로 내 것인 상태예요. 세 들어 사는 집은 점유는 해도 소유는 아니에요. 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 일상에서는 '차지'라는 말을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 점유 is actually holding and using something; 소유 (ownership) is legally owning it. A rented home is in your 점유 but not your 소유. It appears mostly in news and legal talk; in daily speech Koreans lean on 차지 (taking up a space).

p.n: 점거 implies forcible seizure, so it does not fit simply taking up seats.

examples.en: The government decided to make remote work an official system.
Waste decreased after recycling separation was made an official system.

examples.ko: 이 규칙을 제도화하면 모두가 따르기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If we make this rule official, it will be easy for everyone to follow.
The company made parental leave an official system last year.

examples.ko: 좋은 관행을 제도화한 뒤에도 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Problems can still arise after a good practice has been formalized.

examples.ko: 학교에서 이 활동을 제도화하자는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Opinions came up to make this activity an official program at school.

explain: 관행이나 약속을 법이나 규칙 같은 공식적인 틀로 만든다는 점에서 '정해 두다'보다 훨씬 무게가 있어요. 보통 '~을/를 제도화하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일이 저절로 그렇게 되었을 때는 '제도화되다'를 써요. 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
explain_en: It carries much more weight than simply '정해 두다' because it turns a practice or agreement into an official framework like a law or rule. It is usually used as '~을/를 제도화하다', and when things become that way on their own you use '제도화되다'. You often see it in news and reports.

examples.en: The government decided to crack down on illegal ads.
The school took disciplinary action against a student who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 여러 나라가 그 나라를 제재한 뒤 무역이 줄었어요.
examples.en: After several countries imposed sanctions, trade decreased.
Extreme behavior has to be restricted.

examples.ko: 나쁜 말을 쓴 사용자를 제재하는 규칙이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A rule was made to penalize users who use abusive language.

examples.ko: 협회가 선수를 제재하면 경기에 나갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the association sanctions a player, they can't play in games.

explain: 규칙이나 법을 어긴 사람, 회사, 나라에게 불이익을 주어 활동을 막거나 제한할 때 써요. '벌하다'는 벌 자체에 초점이 있어요. 뉴스에서는 '경제 제재'로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when you penalize a person, company, or country that broke rules or laws by limiting or blocking their activity. '벌하다' focuses on punishment itself. In the news you often hear it in '경제 제재' (economic sanctions).

examples.en: The school limits phone use.
The doctor limited how much salt I eat.

examples.ko: 이 길은 큰 차의 진입을 제한하고 있어요.
examples.en: This road restricts entry for large vehicles.

examples.ko: 나이를 제한한 행사라서 저는 못 가요.
examples.en: It is an age-restricted event, so I cannot go.
We take the test with a time limit.
From now on I will limit my game time.

explain: 사람이나 규칙이 양, 시간, 대상에 한계를 정할 때 써요. 명사 '제한'은 '시간 제한', '나이 제한'처럼 자주 써요. 스스로 줄이는 것은 '줄이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a person or rule sets a ceiling on an amount, a time or who may take part. The noun '제한' is common in '시간 제한' and '나이 제한'. When you cut back by yourself, '줄이다' also works.

examples.ko: 이 보고서는 국제 기준에 준거해 작성했어요.
examples.en: This report was written based on international standards.

examples.ko: 심사는 공개된 평가 기준에 준거하여 진행돼요.
examples.en: The screening is carried out in accordance with the published criteria.

examples.ko: 법에 준거하지 않은 계약은 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A contract that does not conform to the law can become a problem.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 업계 표준에 준거한 방식으로 일해요.
examples.en: Our company works in a way that follows industry standards.

examples.ko: 어떤 자료에 준거했는지 출처를 밝혀 주세요.
examples.en: Please state your source and which materials you based this on.
The person in charge explained that it was handled according to the regulations.

explain: 거의 '~에 준거하여/준거해'의 모양으로 쓰고, '~에 따라'를 딱딱하게 말한 느낌이에요. 보고서, 법, 논문에서 주로 보이고 일상 대화에서는 '~에 따라', '~대로'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '~에 준거하여/준거해', a stiff version of '~에 따라'. You mostly see it in reports, laws, and papers, while in daily talk people say '~에 따라' or '~대로'.

examples.en: This street is designated as a no-smoking zone.
My seat has already been assigned.
Please come at the designated time.
That building was designated a cultural heritage site.
I'll let you know once a person in charge is assigned.

examples.ko: 주차는 지정되어 있는 곳에만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only park in designated spots.

explain: 사람이 아니라 장소, 시간, 자리가 주어로 '정해진다'는 뜻이에요. '지정석'(정해진 자리), '지정 장소'처럼 명사 앞에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 '정해지다'보다 공식적으로 정해졌다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: The subject is a place, time, or seat that gets officially set. It often attaches to nouns, as in 지정석 (assigned seat) and 지정 장소. Compared with the plain 정해지다, it sounds more official.

en: official authority; authority of one's office

examples.en: The mayor handled the matter on his own authority of office.
A judge must not abuse his authority.
This is outside my authority.
The chairperson called the meeting on the authority of the post.

examples.ko: 경찰관이 직권을 이용해 개인 정보를 봤다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was news that a police officer used his authority to look at personal information.

examples.ko: 공무원은 자기 직권 안에서만 일을 결정할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A public official can decide matters only within his own authority.

explain: 직무에 따라 주어지는 권한이에요. '직권으로'는 누가 신청하지 않아도 담당자가 스스로 판단해서 한다는 뜻으로 뉴스와 공문서에 자주 나와요. '직권 남용'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 일반적인 '권한'보다 직책에 묶인 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is the power that comes with a job or post. '직권으로' means the person in charge acts on their own judgment without anyone applying, and it often appears in news and official documents. '직권 남용' is also a common phrase. It is tied to a position more strongly than the general word '권한'.

examples.en: City Hall carries out this year's budget.
The police enforced the law fairly.

examples.ko: 회사는 다음 달부터 광고비를 집행할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will start spending its ad budget next month.
We record where all the money being spent goes.
After carrying out the plan, we checked the results.

examples.ko: 판결을 그대로 집행한 뒤 사건이 끝났어요.
examples.en: After the ruling was carried out as it was, the case ended.

explain: 정해 둔 계획, 법, 예산을 권한이 있는 곳이 실제로 실행할 때 써요. '실행하다'는 누구나 하는 일에 쓰지만 '집행하다'는 정부, 회사, 법원 같은 공식적인 곳에서 주로 해요. 뉴스와 공문서에는 많이 나오고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: Used when an authorized body actually carries out a set plan, law or budget. '실행하다' is for anyone, but '집행하다' mostly belongs to governments, companies and courts. It is common in news and official documents and rare in everyday talk.

dis.h: carry out laws, budgets, or sentences

p.n: 실시하다 does not combine naturally with a budget.
